item.title: ‘Just Ridiculous’: A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness
item.description:
Thomas Nagel, a legendary figure in the philosophy of mind known for his famous essay 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?', has shared his views on the current wave of artificial intelligence. Honored this week with the prestigious million-dollar Berggruen Prize for his lifelong philosophical contributions, Nagel addressed the controversial topic of whether advanced chatbots and language models could ever become conscious.
He firmly rejected the notion, describing claims of AI sentience as just ridiculous. According to Nagel, true consciousness is deeply tied to subjective experience and biological existence, elements that are fundamentally missing from silicon-based algorithms and statistical pattern matching. As tech companies and researchers increasingly grapple with the ethical and philosophical implications of lifelike AI, Nagel's stark dismissal serves as a reminder of the vast gap between simulating human conversation and actually feeling it.

item.title: IBM Time-Series Models Run Natively on Confluent for Real-Time Insights
item.description: Background Businesses continuously generate operational data such as machine readings, payments, and inventory changes, but this information often sits across fragmented systems. According to IBM and Confluent, relying on periodic batch processing means forecasts frequently arrive too late to influence outcomes. Details To bridge this gap, IBM's time-series models have been integrated natively inside Confluent Cloud and Confluent Platform for Apache Flink. As stated in the announcement, the models run on standard CPUs without requiring dedicated GPUs. They support functions like forecasting demand, detecting anomalies, and enabling semantic search across streaming data using SQL. Impact The integration aims to help organizations in manufacturing, retail, banking, and airlines make faster operational decisions. Real-world applications include optimizing production setpoints, catching supply chain shortages, and enhancing fraud detection by evaluating individual spending patterns in real time.

item.title: Merck Scraps Centerpiece of $2.7B ArQule Buy After Late-Stage Safety Concerns
item.description:
According to BioSpace, Merck is completely shutting down its BELLWAVE clinical development program for nemtabrutinib (also known as MK-1026 or ARQ 531) following a recommendation from an external data monitoring committee. The committee reviewed findings from the late-stage BELLWAVE-011 trial in untreated chronic lymphocytic leukemia and small lymphocytic lymphoma, concluding that the potential benefits might not outweigh the risks. Consequently, Merck is also terminating the BELLWAVE-008 and BELLWAVE-010 trials.
Originally acquired as the centerpiece of the $2.7 billion ArQule buy at the end of 2019, nemtabrutinib was meant to establish Merck in the non-covalent BTK inhibitor space, where competitors like Eli Lilly have already secured regulatory approvals with drugs like Jaypirca. This discontinuation comes as Merck prepares for upcoming patent expiries for Keytruda starting in 2028, which puts billions in revenue at risk, though analysts remain generally optimistic about its other pipeline candidates.

item.title: Major Clean Energy Deals Announced at RE+ Trade Show
item.description: As the RE+ clean energy trade show unfolds in Las Vegas, several significant transactions have reshaped the battery energy storage system (BESS) landscape. Samsung SDI's Massive LFP Deal Samsung SDI announced a multi-year, 16GWh lithium iron phosphate battery supply agreement with Jupiter Power, running for three years from 2029. The batteries will be manufactured in Indiana, leveraging Samsung SDI's domestic production lines. This brings Jupiter Power's total booked orders with Samsung SDI to approximately 27GWh. EQT Acquires Flatiron Energy Private equity firm EQT's energy transition infrastructure arm reached an agreement to acquire US utility-scale BESS developer Flatiron Energy from Hull Street Energy. Flatiron boasts a 24GWh total pipeline across the Northeast and Mid-Atlantic US, reinforcing EQT's growing global footprint in energy storage alongside its previous investments in Statera and Ju:niz Energy. Canadian Solar Expands Storage Footprint Canadian Solar's BESS subsidiary, e-Storage, signed a 590MW/1,430MWh deal with global developer X-Elio to supply systems for five projects in the US and Australia. The agreement includes 22-year long-term service agreements, underscoring Canadian Solar's strategic pivot as its storage shipments surge while traditional photovoltaic module shipments decline.

item.title: STAT+: FDA Discloses Reasons for Rejecting Summit Drug
item.description: According to reports by STAT reporters Elaine Chen and Adam Feuerstein, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has shed light on the rationale behind its decision to turn down a pharmaceutical product from Summit. Such disclosure provides crucial insight for industry observers tracking how the regulatory agency evaluates clinical data and safety profiles. In the same reporting cycle, other notable updates included the White House pulling the nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the FDA, alongside updates on clinical trials and drug approvals from other major players like GSK, Biogen, and Nuvalent.

item.title: Brazil Receives Parts for Two Quantum Computers from China
item.description:
According to the Brazilian Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation, the equipment arrived on November 16 in João Pessoa, valued at about 83 million Brazilian reais, and was transported to the newly established International Center for Computing and Quantum Technologies (Ciquanta). Around 15 Brazilian researchers will work alongside visiting Chinese specialists starting November 24 to handle the physical structure, cooling systems, and software configuration.
The project aims to transfer technology and train local experts in operating the machines and developing quantum algorithms. While testing is expected to begin in January 2027 pending the arrival of essential cooling supplies like helium-3, actual scientific research projects are slated for the first half of 2027, with officials hoping to decentralize research funding and retain regional talent.

item.title: Revopoint MIRACO 2 3D Scanner Automates Scan-to-CAD Workflows with AI Agents
item.description:
Shenzhen-based 3D scanner manufacturer Revopoint announced the upcoming Kickstarter launch of its MIRACO 2 3D scanner. The standalone 960-gram device features an 8-core CPU, a 6-core NPU, and a 6-inch 2K AMOLED touchscreen, allowing users to handle depth computation and point cloud processing on the go. According to Revopoint, the device supports six distinct scanning modes, reaching single-frame accuracies of up to 0.02 mm in multi-line laser mode.
A key addition is Revo Agents, an AI-native engineering co-pilot that lets users direct complex 3D operations using natural language commands. The system aims to streamline point cloud fusion and scan-to-CAD conversions while keeping user data secure through a local sandbox environment and optional offline functionality.
For advanced use cases, the scanner can connect to a PC via Wi-Fi 6 or USB-C to unlock physically scaled 3D Gaussian Splatting for XR applications. The super early bird pricing for the Kickstarter campaign starts at $1,425.

item.title: Will Wright’s next game uses AI to map your memories
item.description:
Will Wright, creator of *SimCity* and *The Sims*, is working on a mobile social simulation game called *MyMems* through his developer team at Gallium Studios, with a planned launch in 2027. The title allows users to input autobiographical anecdotes by speaking short stories into their mobile devices. Generative AI then processes these narratives to construct interactive environments and populate them with AI-powered avatars representing real-world acquaintances, essentially building a digital map of the player's psyche.
While generative AI faces widespread skepticism and backlash across the gaming industry, including opposition from indie developers and players, the Gallium Studios team believes user reception can remain positive if the technology is applied appropriately. Product manager Anthony Maitz explains that because players continuously author the world piece by piece in a lightweight style, the experience feels organic rather than derivative. Executive producer Virginia McArthur emphasizes that the goal is to create a cozy world builder rather than an automated output generator, following through on the natural tendency players historically showed in *The Sims* to map their own real-life relationships into virtual spaces.

item.title: Mistral AI is not French president's 'personal project,' says CEO
item.description:
Speaking at the Semafor tech conference in California, Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch addressed concerns regarding the startup's political ties and future. When the moderator suggested the company was a personal project of French President Emmanuel Macron and questioned its survival under potential far-right leadership, Mensch strongly rejected the characterization. He stated that the company simply grew rapidly in France while Macron happened to be in office, comparing Macron's backing to how US presidents aggressively promote domestic technology.
Addressing the broader political landscape, Mensch expressed confidence that European support for AI sovereignty would remain strong regardless of upcoming election results, noting that the realization of AI's strategic importance transcends political orientation. He also touched upon the company's financial future, mentioning that Europe would be the natural place for an IPO, though it will not happen this year. Additionally, Mensch criticized certain US AI giants for allegedly using enterprise client data to build competing products.

item.title: Cognizant Wins £133 Million Network Rail IT Contract
item.description: Contract Details According to a notice on the UK government procurement portal reported by Moneycontrol, Network Rail selected Cognizant for a £133.2 million contract (rising to £159.84 million with VAT) after a competitive bidding process that included competitors like Tata Consultancy Services and HCLTech. Scope and Timeline The nearly seven-year engagement is scheduled to run from January 2027 to January 2034. The scope encompasses physical data centres, networks, edge computing rooms, mainframes, and cloud platforms. Background Cognizant has a 13-year relationship with Network Rail, previously collaborating on cloud migration, IT service management, and railway asset management utilizing artificial intelligence and the Internet of Things.

item.title: Australia's Meliora Foods Launches Plant-Based Liquid Egg Made from Mung Beans
item.description:
Meliora Foods, a subsidiary of investment firm My Co, has rolled out a liquid vegan egg alternative utilizing mung bean protein isolate supplied by its sister company, Australian Plant Proteins. The product is designed to pour, scramble, and bake similarly to conventional eggs and is sold in 500ml bottles equivalent to about 11 eggs, priced at A$8.50.
My Co representatives state that the launch aligns with record-high per capita egg consumption in Australia, though the company emphasizes the product was developed over several years independently of recent supply pressures like avian flu. Following its retail debut at Coles, the company plans to target the commercial foodservice sector and expand its product portfolio over the coming year.

item.title: Australian artists react to AI music training at the Aria awards
item.description: During the 2026 Aria awards, nominated artists including Boy Soda, Miss Kaninna, and 3% were interviewed about the contentious issue of AI training on copyrighted music. The discussions follow warnings from Australian music bodies regarding tech companies utilizing local catalogs without consent, alongside high-profile industry figures backing artists in the copyright fight. The conversations emphasize the ongoing tension between rapid technological advancement and creators seeking fair compensation and control over their artistic output.

item.title: Big Pharma tells biotechs: stop spamming on LinkedIn and show all your data
item.description:
Key Takeaways from Big Pharma Deal-Makers
At the Fierce Biotech London Life Sciences Week event, business development leaders from several pharmaceutical giants offered a candid look into how they evaluate potential biotech partners. Juergen Eckhardt from Bayer warned against aggressive sales pitches, noting that spamming on LinkedIn damages trust right from the start. The Importance of Data Transparency
GSK's Tim Egan stressed that biotechs must be completely upfront about their data assets. Trying to hide flaws or withholding negative data will only backfire once the potential partner unearths them during diligence. Representatives from Eli Lilly, Merck, and Johnson & Johnson echoed that the core focus remains on outstanding science and mutual capability-building rather than simply scrambling to patch up patent cliffs.

item.title: Smart Windows Could Cut Heating and Cooling Demand By Managing Heat Across Seasons
item.description: Technical Mechanisms and Performance Researchers are developing active and passive technologies to control heat transfer in glazing. Active methods use electrical stimulation, such as silver nanowire networks and dielectric gel heaters, while passive approaches rely on materials like hydrogen-doped indium oxide and ultrathin MXene coatings to block heat or harvest solar energy. Studies show that specific configurations can achieve high optical transparency while providing effective heating, anti-icing, or radiative cooling. Broad Applications Beyond Buildings Beyond residential and commercial architecture, these thermal-regulating materials have potential uses in automotive defoggers, radiative-cooling films for parked cars, heat management lenses for AR/VR smart glasses, and selectively transparent greenhouse films that lower agricultural water evaporation. Commercial Challenges Despite promising laboratory results and simulation data showing energy savings of up to 34% in HVAC systems, the technology faces hurdles. Most prototypes are limited to small scales, and materials must withstand decades of weather exposure, thermal cycling, and mechanical stress without degrading.

item.title: Google's Gemini 4 Neon leaks, as users joke about the chaotic periodic table naming
item.description: According to model tracking accounts and code snippets found by developers, Google is preparing a new model dubbed Gemini 4 Neon, along with a corresponding TIER_NEON subscription level marked as Gemini Ultra. Since September, Google has rolled out several Gemini 4 models named after chemical elements, including Argon for software engineering, Carbon for agent tasks, and Hydrogen for speed and efficiency. However, the sequence defies standard periodic table order, alphabetical sorting, or cosmic abundance, prompting widespread internet jokes and speculation about whether Google picks names blindly out of a hat. Beyond the confusing naming convention, users have also complained about fragmented access and messy subscription tiers across Google's multiple workspaces, APIs, and consumer apps, making it difficult to keep track of which account actually gets access to the latest features.

item.title: Mitsubishi Electric to Launch Demo Satellite on PLD Space's MIURA 5 Rocket
item.description:
Mitsubishi Electric has finalized a contract with Spanish rocket builder PLD Space to launch a demonstration satellite on the second test flight of the MIURA 5 vehicle. This agreement follows Mitsubishi Electric's financial backing, which includes leading a €50 million investment in March 2026 and a subsequent €108 million extension in September as part of a €180 million Series C round.
The upcoming demonstration flight will support Mitsubishi Electric's plans to develop a large satellite constellation. According to PLD Space, the launch date depends on the outcome of the rocket's inaugural flight, which is currently scheduled for the first half of 2027 from the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana.

item.title: MIT researchers design Lego-like blocks to cut building emissions
item.description:
According to MIT Advanced Manufacturing:
The construction industry contributes heavily to global greenhouse gas emissions partly because buildings consume excessive materials. While engineers know how to design structurally efficient buildings, producing and installing custom parts remains prohibitively expensive. Traditional digital fabrication methods like 3D printing, meanwhile, require extremely high precision and costly machinery.
To solve this, MIT researcher Miana Smith inverted the logic by building complex blocks that absorb errors, comparing the concept to Lego bricks where simple pieces prevent error accumulation. Her team developed larger, internally connected lattice voxels that enable cheap robots with high margins of error to assemble load-bearing structures. According to Smith, this method could cut embodied carbon emissions by roughly 80 percent compared to standard concrete construction, and the team is currently collaborating on housing projects and pursuing a startup focused on sustainable concrete.

item.title: Jimeng Seedance 2.5 Major Update Brings Native 4K Pipeline to AI Video Generation
item.description:
According to fanr's evaluation, Jimeng Seedance 2.5's 4K upgrade addresses major pain points in commercial video production, such as brand TVCs, high-ticket e-commerce displays, and offline large-screen exhibitions. The model supports 10bit BT.709 color format, offering finer color gradations and wider color adjustment room for post-production compared to standard 8bit videos. It also accommodates six different aspect ratios, allowing teams to generate vertical, horizontal, square, and ultra-wide materials from a single creative concept.
In addition to resolution, the update integrates with other Jimeng tools like Seedream 5.5 and Seedance 2.5 Flash, forming a connected production workflow from asset preparation to video generation and editing. Furthermore, Jimeng has launched an enterprise solution aimed at helping corporate teams integrate AI content generation into their daily production pipelines.

item.title: IQM and AMD Demonstrate Hybrid Quantum-GPU Chemistry Workflow
item.description:
According to IQM Quantum Computers and AMD, the two companies have successfully demonstrated an end-to-end hybrid quantum-classical workflow for computational chemistry. The setup splits molecular ground-state energy calculations between IQM's 20-qubit superconducting IQM Garnet processor and AMD Instinct GPUs utilizing the open-source ROCm software stack.
The workflow applies Quantum-Selected Configuration Interaction to handle memory scaling limits. The quantum processor prepares trial circuits and samples bitstrings, while the AMD GPU filters samples and executes matrix diagonalization using JAX on ROCm. The teams validated this pipeline across 17 bond lengths on physical hardware and published the code as an open-source Jupyter notebook.

item.title: World's First Halal-Certified Cultivated Meat Launches in the US
item.description:
According to Good Food Institute APAC:
Following fatwas from Islamic authorities in Singapore, South Korea, and Malaysia recognizing cultivated meat under certain conditions, UPSIDE Foods has secured the first official halal certification for a cultivated meat product. Circle H International, whose standards are recognized globally by major institutions including the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, completed a year-long evaluation of the product.
To meet market demands, UPSIDE's new formulation combines cultivated chicken with plant-based ingredients like soy protein isolate and pea fibre, with cultivated meat making up a double-digit percentage of the final product. The company reports that its revamped production system can produce over 1 million pounds of chicken annually on less than half an acre of land. Early consumer reviews at participating restaurants like Los Angeles' Chimmelier described the product as crispy and delicious.

item.title: October EV Penetration Reaches 64.3% with Over 200,000 Battery Enterprises
item.description:
Data released by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology shows that in October, China's new energy vehicle production and sales reached 2.017 million and 1.94 million units respectively, with the monthly penetration rate hitting 64.3%. From January to October, cumulative production and sales completed 14.509 million and 14.411 million units, with the cumulative market share rising to 54.8%.
This robust growth has strongly driven downstream and upstream segments. According to the China Automotive Power Battery Industry Innovation Alliance, domestic power battery installations reached 576.3 GWh from January to September, while storage battery sales hit 595.4 GWh, representing a significant 112% year-on-year increase. Because battery and energy storage manufacturing processes share high compatibility, production lines can flexibly switch between orders, stabilizing capacity utilization.
Market competition is shifting heavily toward manufacturing execution. Factors such as coating thickness precision, stacking alignment accuracy, and temperature control during formation directly dictate cell lifespan and cost efficiency. With over 202,000 battery-related enterprises nationwide tracked by enterprise database Tianyancha, surviving and thriving in this crowded market relies entirely on long-term technological refinement rather than simple capacity expansion.
